Subject: Request: Technical safeguards for cross-border processing & DPF evidence

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking our call yesterday. As part of our procurement and legal review we need a concise package showing how Redwood meets cross-border transfer expectations for our EU customer data. Specifically our privacy and legal teams asked for the following: 

- A mapping of where customer data is processed (hosted, dedicated, private) and what elements may leave the EU.
- Evidence that transfers to the US are covered (SCCs/DPF) and any additional technical/organizational measures.
- Key custody and encryption details (KMS/HSM, BYOK options).
- A signed or draft DPA annex we can circulate internally.

Can you send a short consolidated packet and flag any items that require legal redlines or DocuSign? We need to finish our RFP checklist by next week.

Best,
Emma

Privacy & Compliance Lead
DataTrust Solutions

Hi Emma — thanks, happy to consolidate. I have attached a transfer map and a controls summary to start (see redwood_transfer_map_v1.xlsx, redwood_controls_summary.pdf). Highlights up-front: 

- Transfer coverage: Redwood supports EU-hosted, Dedicated (customer-region), and Private (VPC/on-prem). For our hosted offering we rely on EU regional processing where requested; transfers to the US only occur for model serving variants if the customer pins a model hosted in the US or requests cross-region routing.
- Legal basis: We operate under controller-processor terms in our DPA. For transfers we implement SCCs and support DPF where applicable; we include technical mitigations (encryption in transit and at rest, strict subprocessor controls).
- Encryption and keys: We offer customer-managed keys (BYOK) via supported KMS integrations; HSM-backed key storage is available for Private deployments.

Next steps: Ben Carter (cc'd) can add the technical validation detail and a short write-up of our DPF supplementary measures. After that I will package a single PDF and a DPA addendum draft for you and share a Drive link + DocuSign preview. Would a 30-minute call Monday 21st work to walk legal through the packet?

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hannah — adding technical specifics that Emma's team typically asks for. Please pull these into the customer packet (I flagged the sections to copy into the controls summary):

1) Transfer map and routing policies
- Hosted API: model-serving may run in EU or US depending on model variant. Customers can request region pinning; default routing is region-aware. For cross-border routing we include logging and explicit record of data flow in the export map.

2) Legal & transfer safeguards
- We support EU SCCs as a baseline (controller-processor + processor appendix). For customers in-scope of DPF we provide a supplemental attestation describing organizational safeguards and technical measures; acceptance of DPF-compatible measures should be confirmed with legal procurement.

3) Technical measures / mitigation
- Transport: TLS1.2+ with forward secrecy.
- At-rest: AES-256 encryption for persisted artifacts; token-level storage uses per-tenant encryption keys in hosted offering.
- KV/prefix caching: minimal retained state; customers can opt-out of caching.
- Keys: Customer-managed keys supported via Google KMS, AWS KMS, and Azure KeyVault. HSM-backed options for Private deployments. BYOK provisioning is supported via our onboarding flow.

4) Operational controls
- SOC 2 Type II coverage (controls and scope documented), regular penetration tests, vulnerability management, and SOC/annual audit reports available under NDA.

5) Residual risk & options
- If DataTrust requires zero outbound transfers, our Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) permits fully EU-resident compute and storage with customer-managed key custody.

Attachments I recommend including in the reply: redwood_dpf_evidence_v2.pdf (summary of measures), redwood_dpa_addendum-draft.docx (DPA annex draft). I also linked our internal technical addendum (kb: dpf_tech_addendum.md) for reference.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
